title.title: Turing machines in forced Navier–Stokes flows
title.subtitle: Claim: for any machine, a smooth force makes a tagged fluid particle reach a region exactly when it halts

plain: Push a fluid with a cleverly designed force and it computes: a tagged drop arrives only if a program halts

beats.text: A compiler turns a Turing machine and its input into a force on the fluid
A tagged particle enters $U$ exactly when the machine halts
The catch: any smooth divergence-free velocity solves Navier–Stokes with this force

steps: Encode the machine's tape as numbers, using generalized shifts
Run each step with smooth shear flows that lose no information
Read the force off the chosen velocity: the fluid computes

achievement.label: Universal computation in forced Navier-Stokes flows
statement: \text{particle enters } U \iff M \text{ halts on } w
achievement.context: Motivated by Tao's fluid-computer programme (JAMS 2016); nothing about unforced fluids or blowup
achievement.note: Nine papers, 258 pages; the force does the work

verify.detail: Lean: six comparator challenges, incl. a compactly supported flow in $\mathbb{R}^3$. Not every paper
verify.ourCheck: We did not build the Lean

voice.text: A compiler turns a machine into a force. A tagged particle arrives when it halts.
Encode the tape as numbers, run each step with shear flows.
Claimed: reaching the region is undecidable, in general.
